stemBlocks.value: Triangles P, Q and R are drawn on a grid: P has vertices (1, 0), (1, -2) and (2, -3); Q has vertices (-1, 4), (-1, 2) and (-2, 1); R has vertices (3, 4), (3, 2) and (4, 1). Describe fully the single transformation that maps (v) triangle P onto triangle R, and (vi) triangle R onto triangle Q.
Think first: Compare matching vertices: if the shape stays the same way round and the same size, look for a translation or rotation; if it is flipped, look for a reflection.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p262-q09 from workbook page 262.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices of the three triangles from the grid.

contentBlocks.value: Take them in the same order around each triangle.

solutionSteps.instruction: Pair the vertices of P with those of R and find the change in coordinates.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Every point moves by the same vector (2, 4)

solutionSteps.instruction: State the transformation P -> R fully.

contentBlocks.value: The same displacement for every point, with size and orientation unchanged, is a translation.

solutionSteps.instruction: Now pair the vertices of R with those of Q.

contentBlocks.value: (3, 4) -> (-1, 4);  (3, 2) -> (-1, 2);  (4, 1) -> (-2, 1). The y-values are unchanged and each x satisfies x' = 2 - x.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify the mirror line by finding the midpoint of an object-image pair.

contentBlocks.value: Midpoint of x = 3 and x = -1 is x = 1; midpoint of x = 4 and x = -2 is also x = 1.
Result: Reflection in the line x = 1

strategyBlocks.value: Read the vertices of each triangle from the grid, pair up corresponding vertices, and see what single rule takes each object point to its image point.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (v) A translation by the vector (2, 4), i.e. 2 units right and 4 units up.  (vi) A reflection in the line x = 1.

whyThisWorks.value: A transformation is identified by what it does to corresponding points. When every image point is the object point plus the same fixed displacement, the transformation must be a translation, and the vector is that displacement. When corresponding points sit at equal distances on opposite sides of a fixed line with everything on that line fixed, the transformation is a reflection, and the mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of any object-image segment.

examTip.value: 'Describe fully' means state the type of transformation AND all of its data: vector for a translation; mirror line for a reflection; centre, angle and direction for a rotation; centre and scale factor for an enlargement.
